correctness.rationale: The exact column seminorm follows from the H_k telescoping basis and S1=1. Each selector's column H_k can change only on the three edges adjacent to k, or two endpoint edges, giving explicit upper bounds; distinct strict-order local configurations realize all bounds. Segment integration extends all chamber estimates to any pair. Positive sine eigenvector of A_m proves the sharp Collatz–Wielandt minimax and uniqueness. n=2 and n=3 boundaries are explicitly treated. Standalone exact enumeration of all strict orderings n=2..7 confirms each claimed sharp weighted formula (103,218 step-column checks), and numeric sine eigenrelations are checked n=3..30; these finite checks are corroboration, not infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The established result is an exact sharp global two-input weighted BV Lipschitz modulus of a nonlinear endpoint-preserving running median, together with a Perron-optimal edge-weight profile. Restrepo–Chacon give one-input variation smoothing; Maragos–Schafer give morphological/order-statistic structure; Suomela gives sliding median algorithmic complexity. Each is materially distinct. Actual published-finding corpus and own historical claims contain related median, linear smoothing, and optimal-weight facts but not this operator and pairwise seminorm. The 1994 full text remains an explicitly stated originality risk.
residual_risks: The 1994 IEEE paper's full three-page text was not obtainable; an implicit stronger two-input estimate might be present, although its abstract only advertises one-input smoothing.
Older nonlinear order-statistic perturbation literature and unindexed lemmas could contain equivalent boundary and weight formulas.
The OA 1987 report was inspected in selected pages, not exhaustive 44 pages; no whole-document noncoverage claim is asserted.

value.rationale: The same nonlinear median that removes one-input variation may amplify variation of perturbations by factor exactly three. The exact two-input sensitivity and unique weighting that minimizes it distinguish smoothing from robustness and quantify the best possible weighted BV stability for arbitrary path length. The four-site example has an attained factor 3 under uniform weights but factor 2 under tuned weights; the full theorem gives a meaningful structural, not merely computational, classification.
